lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1659: "the" is not in the lexicon

Owner, for the second time: "the needs to be pronounced thuh in kokoro."

He reported this once before, and OTA-1146 answered it by rewriting every
consonant-position "the" to the literal string "thuh" before the line reached
the engine. That fix is what he has been hearing since.

⚠⚠⚠ NOBODY EVER MEASURED IT. espeak-ng is installable in this container, and it
is the same phonemizer the app bundles per voice under <voice>/espeak-ng-data.
One command settles the whole question:

    $ espeak-ng -v en-us -q --ipa "The raider swings the rusted blade at the dog."
      plain     →  ðə ɹˈeɪdɚ swˈɪŋz ðə ɹˈʌstᵻd blˈeɪd æt ðə dˈɑːɡ
      OTA-1146  →  θˈʌ ɹˈeɪdɚ swˈɪŋz θˈʌ ɹˈʌstᵻd blˈeɪd æt θˈʌ dˈɑːɡ

⚠ THE ENGINE WAS ALREADY SAYING "thuh". /ðə/ IS "thuh" — the exact sound he
asked for, three times in that sentence, before anyone touched anything. The
respelling replaced it with θˈʌ: the voiceless th of THUMB instead of the voiced
th of THIS, the STRUT vowel instead of a schwa, and STRESSED, because espeak
stresses a monosyllable it has to sound out. An unstressed article became a hard
beat in front of every noun in the game. He was not still hearing the old
problem — he was hearing the fix.

⚠⚠ THE ESCAPE HATCH OTA-1146 WROTE COULD NEVER HAVE WORKED. It said that if the
voicing came back wrong the alternates to try, in order, were "thuh" → "thu" →
"tha". Measured, all three are voiceless and all three are stressed; the ladder
only ever changed the vowel, and the vowel was not the defect:

    thuh → θˈʌ      thu → θˈɜː      tha → θˈɑː      dhuh → dˈiːhˈʌ ("dee-huh")

⚠⚠⚠ AND NO RESPELLING COULD HAVE WORKED, WHICH IS THE REAL FINDING. espeak gives
word-initial `th` its voiceless reading for every word it does not know; voiced
/ð/ at the head of a word survives only in the closed set of function words in
its dictionary. So there is exactly one string that phonemizes to /ðə/ on this
engine, and it is "the" — entry `Found: 'the' [D@2]`, schwa at stress level 2,
with the vowel/consonant switch applied by espeak itself, identical on en-us,
en-gb and en-gb-x-rp. The two hand-maintained exception lists OTA-1146 built for
hour/honest/heir and use/unit/one were reimplementing, in JavaScript, a rule
already present in C and already correct.

THE RULE THIS LEAVES, pinned: this file respells words the phonemizer does NOT
know. Overriding a word it does know is how you create a mispronunciation, not
how you fix one. Before adding an entry, run the word through espeak.

⚠ THE SAME MEASUREMENT CONDEMNED THREE MORE ENTRIES, so I ran every one:

  · doesn't → duzzent    INERT. The entry claimed espeak said "DOSE-ent". Both
                         spellings are dˈʌzənt; it never did. Removed.
  · Zharak  → zah rak    DESTRUCTIVE. The worksheet's own key says zh ≈ the s in
                         "treasure" — and the respelling dropped the h, so the
                         RAW word was closer than the fix. Zharak → ʒˈæɹæk;
                         "zah rak" → zˈɑː ɹˈæk, a plain Z. Now "zhah rak" →
                         ʒˈɑː ɹˈæk: the owner's vowel AND the zh.
  · Tartaria family      A SYLLABLE SHORT OF THE GAME'S OWN NAME. espeak reads
                         `eeu` as the glide /juː/, so "tar taireeuh" said "tar
                         TERR-yoo" and the plural picked up a parasitic t
                         (tˈɛɹjuːnts). Respelled -ea / -ean / -eans → tˈɛɹiə /
                         tˈɛɹiən / tˈɛɹiənz.

⚠⚠⚠ AND THE IPA-OVERRIDE MAP WAS A LOADED GUN BEHIND A BOOLEAN. It held Unicode
IPA, which is NOT what espeak reads between double brackets — it reads its own
ASCII mnemonics:

    [[ðə]] blade  →  "blˈeɪd"       ⚠ THE WORD IS SIMPLY GONE. Silently.
    [[D@]] blade  →  "ðə blˈeɪd"    ✓

So the failure mode of flipping IPA_OVERRIDES_ENABLED was never "Kokoro reads
the brackets out loud" — the old comment's own stated worst case — it was every
Tartaria, Drakova and Aether in the game going SILENT with no error anywhere.
Rewritten in mnemonics, each measured. The flag stays OFF: measuring espeak is
not the same as measuring the device, and that is exactly the distinction this
OTA exists to enforce.

⚠ OTA-1146'S SUITE IS DELETED, NOT REPOINTED, and that is the honest outcome:
its entire premise was the rule that is gone. ota1659 replaces it and inverts
the reproduction — every shape 1146 rewrote is asserted to pass through
untouched, including the vowel-position cases, so the correctness that used to
live in two exception lists is now demonstrated to survive without them. Two
other suites pinned the old behaviour and were repointed with the history kept
beside them (ota1147's article line, loreLexicon's Reclaimers' apostrophe test —
which has now been retargeted twice for a claim, about apostrophes, that never
changed).

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green.
